problem: A lower-density cage must preserve a curved high target and deforming eye or mouth landmarks without twisted correspondence, floating new geometry, or lost boundary shape.
source_observation: The tutorial initializes live Shrinkwrap, builds eye and mouth boundary loops before filling patches, exposes reversed-stroke twists and projection failures, regularizes spacing, and checks normals/seams before finalization.
controlled_failure: Successive eye loops change angular correspondence. The result is connected, manifold, all-quad, and smoothable, yet its wire flow spirals across the landmark and produces worse curvature diagnostics.
correction: Landmark loops keep matched correspondence and lower density, use live pre- and post-SubD projection, remain in an independent LOW_POLY collection, and survive a bend probe without topology failure.
transfer: The loop-first strategy is rebuilt around a pointed mouth opening at 10 radial segments, then stressed by a separate bend probe.
promoted_rule: Build and align deforming landmark loops first, fill outward with consistently directed quads, and verify base wire plus deformation; manifold all-quad status and smooth shading are insufficient.
limitations: bounded facial patches rather than a complete dragon head
0.85 tutorial-stage silhouette gate passes but 0.90 production target remains open
